Unlike single-endpoint assays (e.g., hERG for cardiotoxicity, DILI for liver toxicity), ClinTox aggregates multiple toxicity mechanisms, making it a more complex prediction task.

Clinical toxicity can arise from on-target effects (exaggerated pharmacology at the intended target), off-target effects (unintended activity at other biological targets), or reactive metabolite-mediated toxicity (bioactivation to chemically reactive species that damage proteins, DNA, or lipids). Many clinical toxicity failures involve idiosyncratic reactions — rare, unpredictable responses in susceptible individuals that are difficult to detect in standard preclinical studies.

Structural features associated with clinical toxicity: reactive functional groups that can form covalent adducts with proteins (quinone/quinone imine precursors from anilines and aminophenols, thiophene S-oxidation, furan ring opening to cis-enedials, epoxides from alkene bioactivation, acyl glucuronide formation from carboxylic acids). Features associated with clinical safety: metabolically stable scaffolds with few bioactivation liabilities. Low daily dose requirement (<10 mg/day). Absence of known toxicophores.
